title: SmallRatio: a Lean 4 formalization of the small-ratio formula for Dedekind sums
description:
Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization accompanying J. S. Farland, "The small-ratio formula for Dedekind sums, formalized in Lean" (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23801362). For a prime p and 0 < h < p, the Dedekind sum s(h,p) is governed by the fractions of small height congruent to ±h: the development proves |12 s(h,p) − p Σ ([hv ≡ u] − [hv ≡ −u])/(uv)| ≤ 12 log₂ p + 6, the sum running over the coprime pairs u, v ≥ 1 with uv < p/2. Summed over a set H of residues, for instance a subgroup of odd order, this gives 12 Σ_{h∈H} s(h,p) = p S_H(p) + O(|H| log p) with an explicit constant, where S_H(p) is the signed sum of 1/(uv) over the small fractions u/v in ±H; with the exact formula of Walum and of Louboutin and Munsch this gives M(p,H) = (π²/6) S_H(p) + O(log p/m) for the mean square of L(1,χ) over the odd characters trivial on a subgroup H of odd order and index m. On the way it proves Dedekind reciprocity by counting lattice points, the identities of Euclid's algorithm with the bound n ≤ 2 log₂ k + 1 on its length, the alternating-sum form 12 s(h,k) = Σ_j (−1)^{j+1} k/(r_j q_{j−1}) + E with |E| ≤ 4n, and Legendre's pairing of the small coprime pairs with the steps of the algorithm, by a lattice-basis argument.

The statements are in Challenge.lean. Lean's comparator checks them against the proofs, with the definition bodies compared, and the proofs are replayed in the Lean, nanoda and con-ron kernels. No sorry, no native_decide; standard axioms only. The changes in each version are described in the release notes on GitHub: github.com/jkfarland-bot/SmallRatios/releases.
notes: AI assistance: the Lean code in this record was drafted and repaired by Claude (Anthropic), an AI model, from the statements and proofs of the companion paper "The small-ratio formula for Dedekind sums, formalized in Lean" (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23801362), and compiled locally with lake. Every proof is checked by the Lean kernel, and Comparator replays the solution against the statement file under the Lean, NanoDa and con-ron kernels. The author, Joseph S. Farland, chose the scope, directed the work, and is responsible for its content. No external human reviewer has checked the formalization.
